title: Nanoscale Organic Contaminant Detection at the Surface using Nonlinear Bond Model
content:
Environmental pollution from organic dyes such as Malachite Green (MG) and Rhodamine B
poses significant threats to ecosystems and human health due to their toxic properties. Rapid detection
of these contaminants with high sensitivity and selectivity is crucial and can be effectively achieved
using nonlinear optical methods. In this study, we employ the Simplified Bond Hyperpolarizability
Model (SBHM) and molecular docking simulations to investigate the Second Harmonic Generation
(SHG) intensity of organic dyes on a silicon (Si(001)) substrate for nanoscale pollutant detection.
Our findings demonstrate that SHG can identify organic dyes based on their unique symmetry
features, with simulations and experimental results for MG exhibiting matching SHG intensity
patterns across all polarization angles. Moreover, nonlinear susceptibility analysis revealed good
agreement between SBHM and Group Theory. In addition we also show how the SHG signal of
dye molecules e.g. Rhodamine B can be enhanced through binding with Graphene Oxyde (GO).
Our molecular docking simulation show that Rhodamine B exhibit a strong adsorption affinity of
−10.4 kcal/mol to a single-layer Graphene Oxide (GO) substrate, primarily through π − π stacking
interactions (36 instances) and adopting a perpendicular molecular orientation. Since conjugated
π-electron system contributes to significant nonlinear susceptibility, such a feature can enhance the
SHG signal. Therefore GO-coated silicon substrates can be applied to increase the possibility of
detecting organic pollutants using SHG with interaction distances ranging from 3.75Å to 5.81Å. Our
approach offers valuable applications in nanoscale organic pollutant detection at the surface.
